LOUDON, Tenn., Nov. 18, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Malibu Boats, Inc. (NASDAQ: MBUU), the global leader in performance sport boats, today announced the Malibu Response TXi Worlds Preview, a global series of familiarization events that gives waterskiers the opportunity to get behind the Response TXi with AtmosDrive and experience the boat before competing on it. Running from December 2026 through February 2027, the series stops in Florida, along Australia’s east coast, and at the 2027 IWWF World Under 21 Waterski Championships site in Peru.

As the exclusive official towboat partner of the International Waterski & Wakeboard Federation (IWWF), Malibu will tow all IWWF World Waterski Championships with the Response TXi with AtmosDrive, including the 2027 IWWF World Under 21 Waterski Championships in Peru (Jan. 10–16, 2027), the 2027 IWWF World Waterski Championships in Australia (Feb. 16–21, 2027), and the 2028 IWWF World Over 35 Waterski Championships (Aug. 27–Sept. 3, 2028). The Worlds Preview gives athletes from every nation the chance to ski behind the boat well before they reach the start dock.

Having pulled 13 world records in waterskiing, the Response TXi is built on Malibu’s T-Cut Diamond Hull, allowing it to track precisely and leave a minimal wake. AtmosDrive delivers more of the engine’s pull into every set: jumpers feel it at the ramp, while slalom and trick skiers feel it through every pass. Many of the world’s top skiers have yet to ski behind the Response TXi, and the Worlds Preview is designed to change that by bringing the boat within reach before competition.

In the United States, the series arrives Dec. 18–20 with a three-day event at Champions Lake in Auburndale, Florida. Athletes from every IWWF member federation can ski timed sets in slalom, trick, and jump, with Will Asher joining Malibu representatives and event staff on the dock throughout the event.

In Australia, Malibu Boats Australia brings the Worlds Preview to four venues across Victoria, New South Wales, and Queensland from Dec. 10 through Jan. 22, with priority for Australian Open and U21 team members. Sessions run at Bridgewater, Victoria (Dec. 10–11); Albury, New South Wales (Dec. 18 and 21–22); Marshalls, Queensland (Jan. 14–15), and Stoney Park, New South Wales (Jan. 18–19), with Australian Masters familiarization at Bridgewater on Jan. 22. The same boat will also tow three L-rated tournaments: the Bridgewater Malibu Series, the Albury Jump-Off, and the Australian Masters. For the two weeks before the Worlds, Feb. 1–5 and 8–12, the boat and site at Albury are open to competitors from every nation.

In Peru, two Response TXi boats with AtmosDrive will be at Bujama Lacus, site of the 2027 IWWF World Under 21 Waterski Championships (Jan. 10–16, 2027), for official familiarization Jan. 10–12, ahead of preliminary rounds beginning Jan. 13.

Official familiarization and competition will be towed by:

Brand: Malibu
Model: Response TXi
Engine: Monsoon M6Di 430 HP (6.2 Liter)
Transmission: ZF 1.22:1
Speed Control: Zero Off, latest version
Slalom & Trick Prop: OJ 3090 – 4 Blade – 14 × 14
Jump Prop: OJ 3084 – 3 Blade – 14 × 13

“The work that happens before competition matters,” said Rachael Green, General Manager of Malibu Boats. “The TXi is built to give athletes the consistent pull and performance they need to focus on their skiing when it counts. The Worlds Preview gives skiers the chance to experience that performance firsthand and understand what makes the Response TXi a strong competition platform.”

“Confidence in the boat is what lets you push the limits,” added Will Asher, Malibu Pro Team skier. “I worked with our engineers on AtmosDrive so the pull would be something skiers can count on, pass after pass. When you trust the boat, you stop thinking about it and start chasing what’s possible. I’ll be on the dock in Florida to help skiers find that feeling for themselves.”

“The world is coming to Australian water, and the skiers deserve to know this boat long before it counts,” said Noel Gordon, Manufacturing & Process Engineer at Malibu Boats Australia. “From Bridgewater to Stoney Park, our Open and U21 teams will have the chance to log real sets behind the Response TXi all summer. Then, for the final two weeks, we open Albury to skiers from every nation, so when they reach the start dock, the boat already feels like home.”

The Worlds Preview underscores Malibu’s commitment to athlete development and to advancing waterskiing at every level, worldwide. More Malibu Response TXi Worlds Preview events are to come, and Malibu will announce them once they are planned.

About Malibu Boats, Inc.

Malibu Boats, Inc. (NASDAQ: MBUU) is a leading designer, manufacturer, and marketer of a diverse range of recreational powerboats, including performance sport, sterndrive, and outboard boats. Malibu Boats, Inc. is the market leader in the performance sport boat category through its Malibu and Axis boat brands, the leader in the 20’–40’ segment of the sterndrive boat category through its Cobalt brand, and in a leading position in the saltwater fishing boat market with its Pursuit and Cobia offshore boats and Pathfinder, Maverick, and Hewes flats and bay boat brands. A leading innovator in the powerboat industry, Malibu Boats, Inc. designs products for a growing range of recreational boaters, fishermen, and watersports enthusiasts who make boating a central part of their active lifestyles. For more information, visit www.malibuboats.com, www.axiswake.com, www.cobaltboats.com, www.pursuitboats.com, or www.maverickboatgroup.com.

Fargo, North Dakota--(Newsfile Corp. - November 18, 2026) - SNAPS Holding Company ("SNAPS") announces that it is filing an early warning report (the "Report") under National Instrument 62-103 - The Early Warning System and Related Take-Over Bid and Insider Reporting Issues in respect of its ownership of 14,802,944 common shares ("Common Shares") of Novra Technologies Inc. ("Novra"), representing 29.5% of Novra's issued and outstanding Common Shares.

The acquisition

On June 4, 2025, SNAPS advanced a convertible loan to Novra in the principal amount of US$500,000 under which it had the right to acquire 2,002,944 Common Shares at a conversion price of CA$0.34 per Common Share (the "First Convertible Note"). Immediately before the triggering transaction, assuming conversion of the First Convertible Note, SNAPS would have held 2,002,944 Common Shares, representing approximately 5.7% of Novra's issued and outstanding Common Shares as of January 29, 2026, calculated on a partially diluted basis.

On January 29, 2026, SNAPS entered into a convertible loan agreement with Novra under which SNAPS advanced US$3,200,000 to Novra (the "Second Convertible Note"). The Second Convertible Note bore interest at 1% per annum and was convertible, at the option of either SNAPS or Novra, into up to 12,894,118 Common Shares at a conversion price of CA$0.34 per Common Share, subject to acceptance by the TSX Venture Exchange and approval by Novra's shareholders. Immediately after the triggering transaction, assuming conversion of the First Convertible Note and the Second Convertible Note, SNAPS would have held 14,802,944 Common Shares, representing 41.8% of the 35,420,293 Common Shares issued and outstanding as of January 29, 2026, calculated on a partially diluted basis. SNAPS elected to convert the full principal amount of the Second Convertible Note.

On June 10, 2026, Novra issued 2,002,944 Common Shares to SNAPS in satisfaction of the First Convertible Note for aggregate deemed consideration of CA$681,001. On June 26, 2026, Novra issued 12,800,000 Common Shares to SNAPS in satisfaction of the Second Convertible Note for aggregate deemed consideration of CA$4,352,000. As of the date hereof, SNAPS holds 14,802,944 Common Shares, representing 29.5% of the 50,223,237 Common Shares issued and outstanding.

Purpose of the acquisition and SNAPS's intentions

SNAPS advanced the loans evidenced by the First Convertible Note and the Second Convertible Note as a strategic investment in Novra and subsequently acquired Common Shares upon conversion of those loans. SNAPS identified Novra's "global market reach, engineering excellence, SaaS/cloud proficiency, and wireless technology expertise" as key assets and sought to leverage the relationship to strengthen its position as a driver of innovation in the communications market. The funds advanced by SNAPS increased Novra's working capital and supported existing liabilities, corporate operations and research and development.

SNAPS has also described a potential transformation of Novra from a communications-focused enterprise into a next-generation intelligent-infrastructure and AI/IoT ecosystem provider.

SNAPS may, from time to time and depending on market conditions and other factors, acquire additional securities of Novra or dispose of securities of Novra, in each case in compliance with applicable securities legislation, including the take-over bid requirements of National Instrument 62-104 Take-Over Bids and Issuer Bids. SNAPS has no present agreement or commitment to acquire or dispose of any securities of Novra.

Novra's head office is at 210 - 100 Innovation Drive, Winnipeg, Manitoba R3T 6G2, Canada. SNAPS's address is 16 South 16th Street, Suite 200, Fargo, North Dakota 58103-9495, United States of America. SNAPS is privately held and incorporated under the laws of the State of North Dakota, and its principal business is the ownership and operation of businesses in technology, manufacturing, healthcare and commercial real estate. PORTLAND, Maine, Nov. 18, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Katahdin Trust, a community bank established in 1918 with nearly $1.2 billion in assets, today announced plans to open a full-service branch at 120 Exchange Street in downtown Portland to serve personal and business banking customers. It will be the Bank's seventeenth branch in Maine. Renovations will begin in early 2027, with the opening expected later in the year.

"Katahdin has been supporting Maine communities for more than 100 years, and for nearly two decades, we've been proud to serve customers and communities across southern Maine," said Jon Prescott, President and CEO of Katahdin Trust. "We're excited to become part of the community and build new relationships in Portland. A downtown branch puts us closer to customers who live, work, and do business in the area, making it easier for them to bank with us."

The Portland branch will be Katahdin's third location in southern Maine, joining a full-service branch and its heavy equipment financing affiliate, Maine Financial Group, both on U.S. Route 1 in Scarborough. Katahdin employs approximately 185 people statewide.

The new branch will offer in-person and drive-up teller service, a 24/7 ATM, and private offices for one-on-one meetings. Customers will have access to a full range of personal and business banking services, including checking, savings, home loans, commercial lending, and cash management, along with the convenience of online and mobile banking.

"Banking is still about relationships," Prescott added. "Customers in Portland will be able to walk in, chat with a local banker, and get to know the people helping them reach their goals."

Planning, approvals, and hiring for the new branch are underway. Katahdin will share more details, including an opening date, as the project moves forward.

About Katahdin Trust
Founded in 1918, Katahdin Trust is a community bank serving individuals and businesses through 16 branches across Maine, as well as online and mobile banking. The Bank also offers heavy equipment financing throughout New England through its affiliate, Maine Financial Group. Its parent company, Katahdin Bankshares Corp., is quoted on the OTCQX under the symbol KTHN. Learn more at katahdintrust.com.

WARREN, N.J., Nov. 18, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Tevogen Inc. (“Tevogen” or the “Company”) (Nasdaq: TVGN), a healthcare company focused on combining biopharma, artificial intelligence, and healthcare services to improve the affordability and accessibility of life-saving medicines, today highlighted a significant reduction in liabilities, from $99.9 million for year ended 2023 as reported on Form 10-Q filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (“SEC”) on May 28, 2024, to $14.8 million for the period ended September 30, 2026 as reported on Form 10-Q filed November 16, 2026. Subsequent to September 30, 2026, the Company further eliminated $7.6 million in liabilities related to a loan obligation.

The Company maintains strong insider ownership with an increase from 83% on February 14, 2024, to 92% as of November 16, 2026.

For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, loss from operations decreased 17%, from $21.5 million in the same period of 2025 to $18.0 million. Additional information available in the Company’s 10-Q.

“Fiscal responsibility guides how we manage our obligations and make financing decisions,” said Ryan Saadi, MD, MPH, Founder and CEO of Tevogen. “Retaining majority control keeps decisions about our direction and growth in the hands of our team. This is central to our strategy as we pursue long-term shareholder value and our ambition to redefine the future of medicine.”

About Tevogen

Tevogen is a healthcare company focused on improving the affordability and accessibility of life-saving medicines. The Company brings together three complementary efforts: Tevogen Bio, its biotechnology initiative; Tevogen.AI, its artificial intelligence and technology initiative; and Tevogen Healthcare Services, its emerging healthcare services initiative.

Together, these efforts are designed to create a more integrated healthcare model in which science, technology, and operational efficiency work together to reduce the cost of medication and expand patient access.

MACAU, Nov. 18, 2026 /PRNewswire/ — Epsium Enterprise Limited (Nasdaq: EPSM) ("Epsium" or the "Company"), an importer and wholesale distributor of premium alcoholic beverages in Macau, today announced its unaudited financial results for the six months ended June 30, 2026.

Revenue for the first half of 2026 decreased to $1.47 million from $3.04 million in the prior-year period amid continued weakness in demand and wholesale pricing for premium Chinese liquor in Macau. Gross profit declined to $0.18 million from $0.50 million. Operating loss increased to $0.75 million from $0.69 million, as lower general and administrative expenses only partially offset the decline in gross profit, while net loss narrowed to $0.67 million from $0.70 million, reflecting higher other income.

First Half 2026 Financial Highlights

  • Revenue decreased 51.8% to $1,466,303 from $3,042,988.
  • Gross profit was $175,353, compared with $495,310; gross margin was 11.96%, compared with 16.28%.
  • General and administrative expenses decreased 22.3% to $918,861 from $1,183,240.
  • Operating loss was $748,194, compared with $691,746. Net loss narrowed 4.5% to $667,598 from $699,106. Net loss attributable to Epsium Enterprise Limited was $667,026, compared with $700,372. Basic and diluted loss per share was $(0.05) for each of Class A and Class B ordinary shares in 2026; the 2025 reported loss per Class A ordinary share was $(0.05).
  • Product mix: fine wine accounted for approximately 41% of revenue, compared with approximately 12%; Chinese liquor accounted for approximately 40%, compared with approximately 79%.
  • Balance sheet: as of June 30, 2026, cash was $612,761, inventories, net were $8,255,912 and working capital was $10,579,060, with no bank borrowings.

Management Commentary

"The first half of 2026 remained challenging for premium Chinese liquor in Macau, with continued pressure on both demand and wholesale prices," said Mr. Son I Tam, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Epsium. "We broadened our portfolio toward fine wine and reduced general and administrative costs by more than 20%. Our priorities include converting inventory into cash and exploring new sales channels through Starlight Years."

First Half 2026 Results

Revenue. Sales to gaming and hotel groups decreased approximately 46% to $1,080,050, and sales to the local market decreased approximately 63% to $386,253, as demand for and wholesale prices of premium Chinese liquor remained weak. Sales of Moutai fell to approximately 35% of revenue from approximately 78%.

Gross margin. The decline in gross margin reflected the higher proportion of lower-margin fine wine and continued price competition. Gross margin on sales to gaming and hotel groups narrowed to approximately 15.6% from approximately 22.8%, and local-market sales were realized at approximately breakeven.

Expenses and other income. The decrease in general and administrative expenses reflected lower professional and consultancy fees; the prior-year period included IPO-related costs. Net other income of $82,713 consisted principally of a forgiveness of payable of approximately $78,700 from a supplier on Chinese liquor purchased in a prior period.

Liquidity and Going Concern

Net cash used in operating activities was $1,362,134 for the six months ended June 30, 2026, compared with $1,927,422 in the prior-year period. As of June 30, 2026, cash was $612,761, compared with $1,978,728 as of December 31, 2025. Net inventories were $8,255,912, representing approximately 68% of total assets, and working capital was $10,579,060. Although the Company had no bank borrowings, a substantial portion of its current assets consisted of inventories.

The Company does not expect its operations to generate net positive cash flows over the next twelve months. Management has prepared a twelve-month cash flow forecast, based on current trading levels and assuming no new borrowings or equity issuance. Taking into account cash on hand, expected customer collections and management's plans to realize additional cash from existing inventory, management believes substantial doubt about the Company's ability to continue as a going concern has been alleviated. The amount and timing of cash realized from inventory are inherently uncertain. If management's plans do not generate the expected cash, the Company would seek to reduce operating expenditures and inventory purchases and sell inventory through existing channels; there can be no assurance these measures would be sufficient. Investors should review the going-concern discussion, including management's plans, in the Company's Form 6-K.

Recent Developments

Starlight Years Entertainment Limited, 60% owned by the Company's subsidiary Media Icon Limited, completed its commercial registration in Macau during the first half of 2026. The Company intends to use Starlight Years to pursue entertainment and event-promotion opportunities, including beverage sales at event venues.

Through its Macau operating entity, Companhia de Comércio Luz Limitada ("Luz"), a limited liability company established under the laws of Macau in 2010, Epsium is engaged in the import and wholesale distribution of primarily alcoholic beverages in Macau. On Utility Scam Awareness Day, BBB and northern Illinois utilities urge customers to slow down as scammers use threats and urgency to steal money and personal information

CHICAGO--(BUSINESS WIRE)--The holiday season brings shopping, gatherings, travel and plenty of distractions. It can also create an opening for utility scammers looking to take advantage of busy customers and pressure them into handing over money or personal information. This Utility Scam Awareness Day, ComEd, Peoples Gas, North Shore Gas and the Better Business Bureau (BBB) of Chicago and Northern Illinois urge families and businesses to stay alert for impostors who may call, text, email or show up at the door claiming to represent a utility. Scammers often create a false sense of urgency, including threats to immediately disconnect service, to get customers to act before they have time to question or verify the request.

The message from the BBB and northern Illinois utilities is simple: slow down and verify. ComEd will never demand immediate payment under threat of disconnection, and taking a moment to question a suspicious request can help customers protect their money and personal information.

“Scammers count on creating a sense of urgency so customers act before they have time to question what they’re being told,” said Tom Byrne, director of Security at ComEd. “Our message is simple: slow down. If someone is threatening immediate disconnection, demanding an unusual form of payment or asking for sensitive information, stop the conversation and verify the request directly with ComEd. Taking that extra moment can help protect your money and personal information.”

Utility scams often rely on urgency and fear. A scammer may pose as a utility employee, claim a customer’s account is past due and threaten to immediately disconnect service unless a payment is made. Others may seek personal or financial information, demand payment through prepaid cards, cryptocurrency, or third-party payment apps, or show up at a customer’s door pretending to be a utility worker.

“Scams are getting more sophisticated with new technologies. They are engineered to look and sound just like your trusted utility. Take a moment to think things through and verify contacts,” said Peter Muntaner, Manager of Contact and Support Centers and Claims — Peoples Gas and North Shore Gas. “If you don’t feel right about what the person is saying or if they’re pressuring you in any way, end the conversation. Hang up the phone, close the door, don’t respond to the email. Contacting your utility directly is a great way to confirm legitimacy.”

The BBB reminds customers and businesses to remain vigilant when someone claiming to represent a utility appears at their home or business and threatens to turn off service unless an immediate payment is made.

“Today's utility scammers are becoming increasingly sophisticated, using convincing caller IDs, official-looking messages and even personal account information to make their schemes appear legitimate,” said Steve Bernas, president and CEO of the Better Business Bureau of Chicago and Northern Illinois. “Consumers should understand that a familiar company name on their phone or a professional-looking message is no guarantee they're dealing with the real utility. Never let the appearance of legitimacy replace independent verification.”

Know the signs of a utility scam

The BBB and northern Illinois utility companies encourage customers to watch for common tactics, including:

  • Threats of immediate disconnection. A caller claims your account is overdue and says your electric service will be shut off unless you pay within a short period.
  • Demands for unusual payment methods. Scammers may demand payment through prepaid cash or gift cards, cryptocurrency or third-party payment apps.
  • Requests for sensitive information. Scammers may ask for Social Security numbers, driver’s license information, bank information or other personal details.
  • Door-to-door impostors. Someone posing as a utility employee may appear at a home or business asking for money or account information. Previous scam warnings have also cautioned that an impostor may attempt to lure a customer outside while another individual enters the property.
  • Digital scams. Customers should also be alert to suspicious contacts through texts, emails and online or social media channels as scammers expand beyond traditional phone and door-to-door schemes.
  • AI tactics. Scammers are increasingly using advanced artificial intelligence (AI) to generate highly convincing fake outage and past-due text message alerts. Stay alert and verify any unexpected requests before taking action.
  • Spoofing: Spoofed phone numbers make calls appear to come from a trusted source like ComEd or can be used to send “smishing” text messages. Don’t rely on caller ID or a familiar-looking number. If pressured for payment or personal information, stop and verify using an official phone number or website.
  • Pressure to act immediately. Threatening or aggressive tactics designed to prevent customers from pausing to verify a request are a major warning sign.

Slow Down and Verify

Customers should never provide Social Security, banking or other personal information to someone who unexpectedly contacts them claiming to represent a utility. If someone visits a home or business claiming to be a utility field representative, customers should ask to see company identification before allowing the person inside.

Customers who believe they have experienced fraud should end the interaction and contact local authorities, followed by their utility using a trusted contact number.

SAN FRANCISCO--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Elastic (NYSE: ESTC) today announced that jina-embeddings-v5-text and jina-embeddings-v5-omni models are now available in the Microsoft Foundry model catalog, deploying as a dedicated endpoint in the customer’s own Microsoft Azure environment. Developers building AI agents and search applications on Azure can run the models as dedicated endpoints in their own Azure accounts, bringing highly accurate semantic search and retrieval to their applications without the compute costs of larger models.

Jina AI by Elastic builds small, purpose-built models that rank at or near the top of industry benchmarks. Jina embeddings v5 for text bring high accuracy in a small footprint across more than 100 languages. The models serve as the backbone for the v5 embeddings omni models, which add multimodal support for images, audio, and video over the same languages. In standard benchmarks, Jina embeddings v5 omni models deliver frontier-class results across all four of these modalities. They outperform models up to 20x larger on image benchmarks (MIEB and ViDoRe), lead their size class on audio (MAEB), and compete with video grounding models several times their size (MMEB-v2).

The Jina embeddings v5 model family includes two types of models, each available in two parameter sizes:

  • Text models: jina-embeddings-v5-text-small and jina-embeddings-v5-text-nano are multilingual text embeddings for retrieval, matching, clustering and classification.
  • Omni models: jina-embeddings-v5-omni-small and jina-embeddings-v5-omni-nano add support for images, audio and video, all in one vector space, allowing unified cross-modal search with a single query.

“AI applications succeed or fail on retrieval, and the best embedding model is the one a team can run where its data already lives,” said Han Xiao, vice president of AI, Elastic. “Bringing Jina embeddings v5 to Microsoft Foundry means teams building on Microsoft Azure can add accurate multilingual, multimodal retrieval to their AI agents and search applications, running in their own Azure accounts, without the compute costs of larger models.”

Big Boy No. 4014 and Living Legend No. 844 to make public appearances in Greeley and Denver in support of Make-A-Wish Foundation

OMAHA, Neb.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Union Pacific’s Big Boy No. 4014 and Living Legend No. 844, the world’s largest and fastest operating steam locomotives respectively, will make two public appearances in Colorado this weekend as part of their first-ever holiday excursion.

The iconic locomotives will stop in Greeley on Saturday morning before arriving at Denver Union Station, where Santa Claus, Mrs. Claus and several elves will be handing out limited-edition gifts while they last during a festive holiday celebration. The sold-out tour has raised more than $150,000 to support the Make-A-Wish Foundation, including a donation from Union Pacific’s Community Ties Giving Program.

The excursion marks several notable milestones. It is the first holiday tour for either locomotive and No. 844’s first public tour since 2019, when it teamed up with Big Boy during the 150th anniversary celebration of the driving of the Golden Spike in Utah.

Big Boy’s return to Colorado follows its historic coast-to-coast tour this summer that captivated millions and wraps up a year-long celebration of America’s 250th birthday.

Saturday, Nov. 21 - Public Viewing Opportunities

Whistle-Stop

  • 10-11 a.m. MST | Greeley, Colorado | 10th Street Crossing

Display Day

  • 3-7 p.m. MST | Denver Union Station

Built in 1944, No. 844 is the last steam locomotive constructed for Union Pacific and the only Class I steam locomotive in North America never retired. After diesel locomotives assumed passenger service duties in the mid-1950s, No. 844 was reassigned to freight and eventually moved into special services in 1960, including steam excursions. It was never scrapped, preserving its place as one of railroading’s most enduring icons capable of reaching speeds of over 100 mph.

Union Pacific reminds rail fans to keep safety top of mind and stay at least 25 feet from railroad tracks and equipment when photographing or viewing the locomotives. Also, never trespass on private property, never stand on railroad tracks or ballast to take photos or videos and never climb on railroad equipment.

ABOUT UNION PACIFIC

Union Pacific (NYSE: UNP) delivers the goods families and businesses use every day with safe, reliable and efficient service. Trains are the most environmentally responsible way to move freight, helping Union Pacific protect future generations. More information about Union Pacific is available at www.up.com.

CONROE, TX / ACCESS Newswire / November 18, 2026 / Olenox Industries Inc. (NASDAQ:OLOX) ("Olenox" or the "Company"), an integrated energy and infrastructure company, today announced that the Railroad Commission of Texas has issued Olenox Corp. Permit No. 10822, a Permit to Operate a Pipeline in Texas, authorizing operation of the Company's central Texas natural-gas pipeline system.

The permit follows a regulatory process that extended for more than one year and represents a major operating milestone for Olenox. With the permit now issued, the Company can move forward with the staged activation, restoration and expansion of the pipeline system while pursuing new natural-gas supply and power-generation opportunities.

The permit covers 95.19 miles of pipeline across Brown, Coleman and McCulloch counties and classifies the system as a gas utility. Olenox Corp. is identified as the pipeline owner, operator and economic operator. The permit was issued October 30, 2026 and is valid through May 31, 2028.

Olenox is currently working to secure an initial natural-gas capacity of approximately 1 million cubic feet per day ("MMcf/d") for the system. The Company plans to use that initial capacity to support the staged deployment of a 4-megawatt ("MW") containerized power-generation site, with initial power production targeted for the first quarter of 2027.

"Receiving this permit is a significant step forward for Olenox and the result of more than a year of regulatory and operational work," said Mike McLaren, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Olenox. "We can now begin moving this pipeline from an existing infrastructure asset into an operating platform for natural-gas transportation and distributed power generation. Our initial objective is to line up approximately 1 MMcf per day of gas capacity, deploy the first 4 MW site and build from there as pipeline throughput and market opportunities increase."

The initial 4 MW site is expected to serve as the first deployment under Olenox's broader strategy to develop multiple containerized power projects of 10 MW or less across the United States and Canada. The distributed model is designed to place scalable generating capacity near available energy resources and expand individual sites in stages as gas supply, infrastructure and customer demand support additional capacity.

Olenox intends to evaluate additional gas-supply arrangements, pipeline restoration requirements, compression and facility upgrades, and future off-take and power-generation opportunities across the system. As throughput increases, the Company expects to assess additional containerized generation deployments that could extend the economic value of the pipeline and its surrounding energy infrastructure.

The planned 1 MMcf/d capacity, 4 MW deployment, Q1 2027 production timeline and future project expansion are targets and have not yet been achieved. Development remains subject to securing gas supply, generation equipment, financing, site readiness, engineering, construction, interconnection, applicable permits and approvals, and other customary operating requirements.
